title: Daring Five-Minute Art Heist in France!
summary:
Imagine sneaking into a museum, cutting through a fence with an electric saw, and grabbing paintings worth millions—all in the time it takes to eat a snack. That's exactly what happened in the south of France early on September 8!

Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer. They used an electric saw to cut through the museum's outside fence and also to cut the clips that held the paintings on the wall. The museum's alarm went off, and police came quickly. The thieves ran across the garden, dropping two of the four paintings they had taken. But they still got away with two paintings by the famous artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir.

Renoir was an Impressionist painter who lived long ago. The stolen paintings are called "Madame Colonna Romano" and "Jeune femme au puits" (which means "Young Woman at the Well"). They were painted around 1910 and 1886. The thieves also tried to take two other paintings but left them behind.

The mayor of the town, Bryan Masson, said the thieves were "well equipped and well informed." The whole operation lasted only five minutes! The paintings are worth at least €9 million—that's over $10 million! That's a lot of money, enough to buy thousands of ice cream cones.

Police are looking for the thieves and the missing paintings. But the museum is close to the Mediterranean Sea, which might make it easier for the thieves to escape.

This isn't the only museum robbery lately. Just two weeks ago, someone stole a diamond necklace from a museum in Vienna. And in March, another Renoir painting was stolen in Italy. Museums are working hard to keep their treasures safe, but these thieves are tricky!
why_it_matters: When a valuable painting is stolen, it may disappear from public view for years, which means fewer people, including kids, can ever enjoy seeing it in person.
